_comment: English narration for the video. segments[k] is the line spoken at build step k, and the counts map 1:1 to the deck's build steps — do not change them. v2 rewrite — context, then evidence, then response, instead of a list of one-liners. The slides that carry the argument (00, 01, 03, 04, 05, 10) keep full sentences; the slides whose screen explains itself (02, 06, 08, 09) are trimmed to captions to buy the time back. budget here is this video's per-segment target and is separate from the deck's data-dur, which is the 3:30 plan for a live presenter. Andrew runs about 15 characters per second at +0%.

segments: Copilot opens pull requests far faster than teams can verify them, and they reach production unverified. We built The Last Human to get from agentic coding to trusted agentic coding.
Agentic AI rests on one premise above all others.
AI has to stay under human control.
Without that, we lose permission to operate at all.
And the method proposed is observability at every layer.
Agents are already in every stage of the SDLC.
Copilot writes the implementation,
tests and review run automatically,
deploy and operate leave records too.
Merge alone records nothing.
The load lands here.
This judgment has been left to intuition. Everyone predicted AI would make them faster.
Measured, they were nineteen percent slower. Self-report is not evidence.
The gaps in agentic coding are already being measured.
A paper this year analyzed twenty-three thousand agentic pull requests.
Descriptions often did not match the code, and twenty-eight percent of those PRs were approved anyway.
The authors call for a mechanism to verify this.
We took that as our starting point and built one.
Parts of the industry answered by banning AI contributions.
Simple, but it gives up the productivity along with the risk.
Instead of banning, we verify only the risky changes and keep the understanding.
So we reversed the direction of explanation.
Other tools have the model explain.
Here the person answers the model.
And that answer binds to the commit.
Let me show you it working.
We put this gate on our own pull requests first.
It fired on twenty-six, and fifteen of them stopped.
Every file carrying judgment stopped us.
Deleting authentication code stays under the threshold.
And twelve merged while pending. We report that too.
This is the path one pull request travels.
Actions recomputes the risk itself.
Below the threshold it merges with no check.
Above it, the author answers from the code.
The receipt binds to the commit.
Only a match opens the gate.
The server's word alone is not enough.
Adoption runs on three tracks.
An operator stands up the server once,
three files per repository, required check last.
The author answers two questions.
There are no long-lived secrets.
AI cannot take responsibility, but a person can.
For that, understanding has to be on record.
Not slowing down, but raising the speed we can carry.
It is running on this repository right now.
AI-generated code. Human-owned decisions.
